findings.title: Full coverage: every success criterion has a home task, every task traces to the design
findings.description: All 18 success criteria map to tasks as tabled above, test tasks follow their implementation tasks (1→1.2, 2→2.2, … 13→13.2), the consolidated failure matrix (Task 14) immediately follows the command task it covers and is mandated by the design's Testing section rather than duplicating unit coverage, and the task sequence matches the design's "Implementation Notes → Order" list (parsers → git helpers → extraction → refusals → inputs → assembly → body → command → guards → live verification). Effort distribution (~2–6 per task, 17 tasks) is proportionate to a slice this size; nothing is oversized and nothing is granular enough to merge.

findings.title: "Needed by" references in Tasks 1 and 2 name the wrong first consumer
findings.description: Task 1 says it is "needed by Task 9" and Task 2 "Needed by Tasks 9 and 10", but neither `parse_slice_branch` nor `parse_task_items` is called by assembly (Task 9 copies fields from `PrInputs`; nothing is parsed there) or directly by the composer (Task 10 receives facts). The first and only caller of both parsers is Task 7's `gather_inputs` (7.1 calls both explicitly). The stated dependency direction is still correct — nothing downstream runs before Tasks 1–2 land — but a junior implementer reading "needed by Task 9" could infer assembly can directly follow the parsers, when the intervening Tasks 3–8 are required. Wording fix only: cite Task 7.

findings.title: Design-internal contradiction on the title's source; tasks resolve it in the correct direction
findings.description: D4a and its task (10a.1) say the middle title term comes from the design's H1 (`# Slice Design: {name}`, prefix stripped), explicitly **not** the frontmatter `slice` field — which is the kebab-case slug. But the Design Review Response's F009 paragraph says the name comes "from the design's frontmatter". The task file implements the D4a reading and even calls out the distinction, so implementation is unaffected; the stale sentence in the review-response summary should be corrected whenever the design document is next touched, since it is the opposite of the specified behavior.

findings.title: No `**Commit**:` markers in the task file — acceptable, but a deviation from sibling files' house style
findings.description: The file carries no `**Commit**:` lines, which is explicitly acceptable and does not block. For context, every comparable task file in this initiative and its predecessors (e.g. `384-tasks.post-findings-to-the-pr.md`'s siblings, `128-`, `144-`–`147-`, `153-tasks.*.md`) places `**Commit**:` markers at working, tested points. If the project's convention for task files is taken to include them, adding them at the tested sub-task boundaries (e.g. after each `x.2` test item) would match the house style; per instructions this is not required, and committing at least once per task remains covered by the project guidelines the implementing agent already follows.
